A workaround that stops the nvlog.nvlgstg writes and keeps the NVIDIA App working, plus details that may help the team find the cause.

System: RTX 4090, Windows 11, driver 621.24, WD SN850X 2TB.

Measured at idle, using the I/O write counters for NVDisplay.Container.exe over 60-second windows: 2.0–2.7 GB per minute (about 120–160 GB/h) after roughly 43 h of uptime. It rewrites the same ~20 MB C:\ProgramData\NVIDIA Corporation\nvtopps\nct\nvlog.nvlgstg in a loop. Turning off logging in the NVIDIA App changed nothing. A fresh service restart starts lower (about 1 GB/min) but climbs as the file grows.

Root cause, from the container's own log: only one plugin writes this file, _nvtopps.dll ("NvTopps_Plugin"), and the container loads it as an OPTIONAL plugin.
Then restart the "NVIDIA Display Container LS" service, or reboot. %ProgramData%\NVIDIA\NVDisplay.ContainerLocalSystem.log then shows "Disable loading of plugin ...\_nvtopps.dll". Writes went to 0 MB per minute, nvlog.nvlgstg is no longer created, the service stays on Automatic, and the NVIDIA App works (refresh-rate change tested). To undo it, delete the _nvtopps key. A driver reinstall may reset it.
The read-only trick didn't work here: on restart the container renamed the read-only file to nvlog_0.nvlog and created a fresh nvlog.nvlgstg.
It would be great to get a fix in the next driver.

Not reproducible here: NVDisplay.Container.exe / nvlog.nvlgstg writes on 621.14 and 621.24. A non-affected data point, posted to help narrow down the trigger.

- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti (16 GB)
- CPU: Intel Core i9-10850K (stock), 32 GB DDR4-3200, 500 GB NVMe
- Display Configuration: 1x MSI MAG 275UPD E14 (27"), 3840x2160, DisplayPort, G-SYNC on
- Operating System: Windows 11
- Driver Regression: none observed. 621.14 (clean install, 2026-11-04) and 621.24 (Express upgrade over 621.14, then a reboot) both behave like the 621.01 rate reported as unaffected in this thread.
- Affected Applications/Games: none. Tested at the desktop idle, with the NVIDIA overlay open, in Edge with a YouTube video playing, alt-tabbing, and (on 621.14) in a game.
- Issue Description: I tried to reproduce the reported continuous rewriting of C:\ProgramData\NVIDIA Corporation\nvtopps\nct\nvlog.nvlgstg.
  621.14: about 45 min of gaming with the overlay on and frequent alt-tabbing. The file stayed at 1.1 MB, last modified 9:46 AM, unchanged throughout. NVIDIA Container processes: 0 MB/s disk.
  621.24: the installer reset the file to 17 KB. After the reboot: 19 KB at 10:44, 26 KB at 11:00 (about 0.4 KB/min) across idle, the overlay, Edge + YouTube and alt-tabbing. Each small increase coincided with an application launching. NVDisplay.Container.exe did not appear among Resource Monitor's disk writers at any point. The only NVIDIA write observed: nvcontainer.exe (NVIDIA App) at about 50 KB/s while the overlay was open; the log did not change.
  Possible differences from the detailed affected report earlier in this thread (an RTX 4070 SUPER with a single 1080p 144 Hz DisplayPort display): GPU generation (50-series here), 4K resolution, G-SYNC on, and a clean install of 621.14. Offered as leads, not conclusions.
- Steps to Reproduce (what I did): 1) Note the size and Date modified of nvlog.nvlgstg. 2) Idle at the desktop 5+ min. 3) Open the NVIDIA overlay; alt-tab repeatedly. 4) Open Edge, play a YouTube video, alt-tab. 5) Re-check the file (F5) and Resource Monitor > Disk. NVIDIA Control Panel / App: default settings, overlay enabled.
